title: Land of Many Rulers
question: Who held the land between the two rivers, and in what order?
hook: One stretch of river country passed from empire to empire.
idea: Mesopotamia passed from Sumerians and Akkadians through Assyria and Babylon to Persian, Greek and Parthian rule.

beats.prompt: Put these events in Mesopotamian history in order.
items: Sargon of Akkad's rise to power (around 2350 BC)
The Neo-Assyrian Empire's control of the Near East (900 to 612 BC)
Conquest by Cyrus the Great (539 BC)
Conquest by Alexander the Great (332 BC)
beats.explain: The sources date these in this sequence: Sargon around 2350 BC, the Neo-Assyrians from 900 to 612 BC, Cyrus in 539 BC, then Alexander in 332 BC.

beats.prompt: Alexander the Great has died, and his successors fight over Mesopotamia. Who comes out on top?

choices.label: The Parthian Empire
choices.feedback: The Parthians held the area around 150 BC, but only after the fight between Alexander's successors was settled.

choices.label: The Sassanid Persians
choices.feedback: The Sassanids took the eastern regions in 226 AD, centuries later.

beats.explain: Of Alexander's successors, the Seleucids emerged victorious; the Parthians and Sassanids came later.

beats.prompt: Match each ruler or group to what it is tied to.
beats.explain: Each leader is linked to the empire or power that rose or won under him.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Mesopotamia means the land between rivers.
So it lies between the Tigris and Euphrates, roughly in modern Iraq.
Nothing beyond modern Iraq was ever part of it.
After the Muslim conquests, names like Syria, Jazira and Iraq were used to describe the region.
beats.explain: In the broader sense, Mesopotamia also includes parts of present-day Iran, Turkey, Syria and Kuwait.
